meta.about: cf: annual capacity factor of U.S. utility-scale generators in 2025 (EIA, final). firm: the ELCC class rating PJM applies in its 2028/2029 Base Residual Auction, the share of a resource's MW that PJM counts toward its adequacy requirement; one market and one auction, not a universal technology value. jobs: the lesson's reference sort, 'yes' (does this job well), 'partly' (depends on the plant, the place or the rules; either answer is accepted) or 'no'. Neutral wording: each reason states the evidence, not a preference.

jobs.label: Cheap energy
jobs.question: Can it fill the year with many MWh at a low running cost?

jobs.label: Firm capacity
jobs.question: Will it be there in the riskiest hours, whatever the weather?
jobs.measure: Firm share: the part of its MW a grid counts at the peak

jobs.label: Flexibility
jobs.question: Can it raise or lower its output quickly when asked?
jobs.measure: Ramp rate, start-up time and how long it can keep going

tech.label: Nuclear
tech.how: Steam from the heat of splitting uranium spins a turbine.

why.energy: Ran at 91.1% of its size in 2025, with a low running cost.
why.firm: PJM counts 96% of its MW, the highest of any class.
why.flex: It can change output within limits, but U.S. plants mostly run flat out.

tech.label: Gas combined-cycle
tech.how: A gas turbine, plus a steam turbine driven by its hot exhaust.

why.energy: Ran at 58.7% in 2025; its running cost moves with the gas price.
why.firm: PJM counts 78%: fuel on demand, though cold snaps can cut the gas supply.
why.flex: It follows demand within a ramp limit and above a minimum output.

tech.label: Gas peaker
tech.how: A gas turbine on its own: quick to start, less efficient.
tech.firmNote: 79% with a second fuel on site

why.energy: Ran only 13.6% of 2025: it costs too much to run for bulk energy.
why.firm: PJM counts 67%, or 79% with a second fuel on site: it is there when called unless fuel or cold fails.
why.flex: Starts quickly and jumps to any level, as in lesson 0.

tech.label: Wind
tech.how: Blades turn a generator; output follows the cube of the wind speed.

why.energy: No fuel: 33.8% in 2025 still adds up to many MWh at almost no running cost.
why.firm: PJM counts 34% for onshore wind: calm spells can fall on the riskiest hours.
why.flex: It can be turned down, but not up: the wind decides.

tech.label: Solar
tech.how: Panels turn sunlight straight into electricity.

why.energy: No fuel: 24.0% in 2025, all of it in daylight.
why.firm: PJM counts 7% for fixed panels and 10% with tracking: little output in the riskiest hours.
why.flex: It can be turned down, but not up: the sun decides.

tech.label: Battery
tech.how: Stores electricity when it is plentiful and returns it later.

why.energy: It makes no energy: the U.S. fleet gave back 82% of what it took in (2019 data).
why.firm: PJM counts 59% for a 4-hour battery and 71% for 8 hours: it runs out if the peak lasts long.
why.flex: Switches between charging and discharging almost at once, within its MW limit.

tech.label: Hydro
tech.how: Falling water turns a turbine; a dam can hold water back.
tech.firmNote: plants without a reservoir; reservoir plants rated one by one

why.energy: No fuel: 34.4% in 2025, limited by the water that arrives.
why.firm: A reservoir can save water for the peak; river plants follow the flow (PJM: 35%); droughts cut both.
why.flex: Reservoir plants raise or lower output quickly; plants without one follow the river.

tech.label: Geothermal
tech.how: Steam or hot water from deep underground drives a turbine.

why.energy: Steady heat and no fuel to buy: 65.9% in 2025.
why.firm: Its heat does not depend on the weather, so it is there at the peak (no PJM class rating to quote).
why.flex: Usually runs steadily; some plants can follow demand within limits.

tech.label: Demand response
tech.how: Users agree to cut or shift their use when the grid asks.

why.energy: It makes no energy: users skip or shift some of their use.
why.firm: PJM counts 91%: users commit to cut when called, within agreed limits.
why.flex: Quick to call, but each programme limits how often and for how long.
